There is prior, well-documented history of a **different-but-related** AttributeGraph/App Hang pathology in this exact codebase (`WORKROOM-2B`), previously fixed in the History/Changes panels by removing per-row `@ObservedObject` subscriptions to `TerminalSessions`. ### 1. `WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:17` (`tabs: [TerminalTab]`, plain `let`) — fed from `WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:508` (`func tabs(for:) -> [TerminalTab]`)
- **Wrapper**: plain `let` property on a non-`Equatable` `View` struct (no `.equatable()` anywhere — verified via grep). Fed from `TerminalSessions`, an `ObservableObject` whose relevant dicts are `@Published` (`WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:337-344`).

- **Value type**: `TerminalTab` is explicitly a `struct` (`WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:14`), and the type's own doc says why: *"`TerminalTab` stays a value type on purpose: a live-title/progress/preview update mutates a copy and reassigns the dict, which is what drives `@Published`."* Each `TerminalTab` carries a `content: TabContent` enum (title strings, diff/file descriptors, etc.) plus override fields — a nontrivial struct that AG must walk field-by-field with no fast identity/pointer shortcut.
- **Frequency**: `TerminalSessions` republishes **per terminal title/activity write** — this is documented directly as the root cause of the prior `WORKROOM-2B` hang (`WorkroomApp/Views/ChangesPanel.swift:729-732`, `WorkroomApp/Views/HistoryPanel.swift:9-30`). 549	        // The focused tab's title is brighter (full primary) so it reads as selected; unfocused titles

551	        // title and nudges the chips sideways. Unread activity (accent) overrides either, on any tab.
552	        .foregroundStyle(
553	          hasActivity ? theme.tokens.accent : (isActive ? Color.primary : theme.tokens.fgMuted)

558	        .truncationMode(.tail)
559	        // Cap the title (~25 chars at `.callout`) so a long name (a file path, a shell-set terminal

561	        // full title rides in the chip's `.help` tooltip below. A short title stays tight (leading

570	    .padding(.trailing, 4)  // tighter than the leading inset — the ✕ sits near the chip's edge
571	    .padding(.vertical, 6)

595	      GeometryReader { geo in
596	        Color.clear.preference(key: TabWidthKey.self, value: [tab.id: geo.size.width])

598	    }
599	    // Only the focused tab is outlined: unfocused tabs have a transparent border so they recede into
600	    // the strip, and the focused tab's outline is a stronger stroke (`fgDim`, not the old `border`
601	    // hairline) so it reads as clearly selected rather than washed out. Grouped tabs are framed by the
602	    // shared `splitWell` bracket instead, so they skip it.

609	    // Hairline centred in the gap between this chip and its left neighbour, so it sits cleanly between
610	    // the tabs and never overlaps either pill. The gap is the HStack's `tabSpacing` (4pt); the overlay

632	    // The full, untruncated name as a tooltip — so a tail-truncated chip still reveals it on hover.

642	    .scaleEffect(isDragging ? 1.04 : 1)
643	    .shadow(color: .black.opacity(isDragging ? 0.25 : 0), radius: isDragging ? 6 : 0, y: 2)
644	  }

# Fix Sentry WORKROOM-2S: App Hang in DiffViewer's AttributeGraph compare

```
_ArrayBuffer.count.getter
_ArrayBuffer.count.getter
infix (==)
AGDispatchEquatable
AG::LayoutDescriptor::Compare::operator()
AG::LayoutDescriptor::compare
AGGraphSetOutputValue

AG::Subgraph::update
GraphHost.runTransaction
ViewGraph.updateOutputs
```

This is AttributeGraph's generic attribute-set comparison: whenever a tracked value (a `@State`
write, or any AG-tracked View input) is set, `AGGraphSetOutputValue` → `LayoutDescriptor::compare`
walks the value's type layout and dispatches to each field's own `Equatable` conformance when one
exists (`AGDispatchEquatable`), falling back to layout descent otherwise. `_ArrayBuffer` is Swift
Array's storage class specifically (not Dictionary/Set), so the two stacked
`_ArrayBuffer.count.getter` frames mean AG was comparing **two nested nested Arrays** — an outer
array's `==` calling `count` on both sides, descending into an element that is *itself* an
Equatable struct containing another Array, whose `==` calls `count` again one level deeper.

documented at `WorkroomApp/Views/HistoryPanel.swift:9-30`): many `HistoryRow` views re-running

many views re-rendering); this is a different mechanism — **one view's `@State` write forcing an
expensive equality walk** — so the earlier fix (resolve-once + `.equatable()`) doesn't apply here.


```swift
// or

```

LoadState` partly is — `.loading` vs `.loaded` differs by case, so *that* write is cheap; the
enum's discriminator short-circuits before AG ever descends into the associated `UnifiedDiff`),
